s: Law is very difficult (to practise according to true faith)

s: monk should practice austerities (day and night in the true religion)
q: I keep clear of the (superstitious) questions and the spells of laymen, exerting myself day and night (in the true religion). Thinking thus, one should practise austerities.

s: men are noble (when born in such families)
q: He will have friends and relations, be of good family, of fine complexion, healthy, wise, noble, famous, and powerful. (18)

s: men are famous (when born in such families)
q: He will have friends and relations, be of good family, of fine complexion, healthy, wise, noble, famous, and powerful. (18)

s: men are powerful (when born in such families)
q: He will have friends and relations, be of good family, of fine complexion, healthy, wise, noble, famous, and powerful. (18)

s: men obtain true knowledge (after enjoying the unrivalled pleasures of human life, through pure religious merit acquired in a former life)
q: After having enjoyed, at their proper time, the unrivalled pleasures of human life, he will obtain true knowledge by his pure religious merit acquired in a former life. (19)

s: true knowledge is obtained by men (through pure religious merit acquired in a former life)
q: After having enjoyed, at their proper time, the unrivalled pleasures of human life, he will obtain true knowledge by his pure religious merit acquired in a former life. (19)

s: Karman is ceased by living beings (leading perchance to a pure state and birth as men)
q: But by the cessation of Karman, perchance, living beings will reach in due time a pure state and be born as men. (7)

s: Karman is shaken off by penances (the remnant)
q: Perceiving that the four requisites are difficult to obtain, he will apply himself to self-control, and when by penances he has shaken off the remnant of Karman, he will become an eternal Siddha. (20)

s: the universe is peopled by living beings (manifold creatures)
q: The universe is peopled by manifold creatures, who are, in this Samsâra, born in different families and castes for having done various actions. (2)

s: living beings are born in different families and castes (in Samsâra, for having done various actions)
q: The universe is peopled by manifold creatures, who are, in this Samsâra, born in different families and castes for having done various actions. (2)

s: living beings undergo non-human births (when bewildered through the influence of their actions and distressed and suffering pains)
q: Living beings bewildered through the influence of their actions, distressed and suffering pains, undergo misery in non-human births. (6)

s: living beings reach pure state (perchance, by the cessation of Karman, in due time)
q: But by the cessation of Karman, perchance, living beings will reach in due time a pure state and be born as men. (7)

s: Fourth Lecture is about Impurity
q: Fourth Lecture. Impurity.

s: Samsâra is lived in by men
q: If a man living in the Samsâra does an action for the sake of somebody else, or one by which he himself also profits, then, at the time of reaping the fruit of his actions, his relations will not act as true relations (i.e. will not come to his help).

s: wealth does not protect carelessness (in this world and the next)
q: Wealth will not protect a careless man in this world and the next.

s: right way is not seen carelessness (though he had seen it)
q: Though he had seen the right way, he does not see it, even as one in the dark whose lamp has suddenly been put out.

s: monk is a Sramana
q: A Sramana who again and again suppresses the effects of delusion, and controls himself, will be affected in a rough way by external things; but a monk should not hate them in his mind.

s: monk is watchful always (like a Bhârunda bird)
q: Though others sleep, be thou awake! Like a wise man, trust nobody, but be always on the alert; for dangerous is the time and weak the body. Be always watchful like a Bhârunda bird!

s: monk steps carefully life (supposing everything to be a snare)
q: A monk should step carefully in his walk (i.e. in his life), supposing everything to be a snare for him.

s: monk cares for life (until enlightenment is won)
q: First he must bestow care on his life till he wins the stake (viz. enlightenment), and afterwards he should despise it, annihilating his sins.

s: human life cannot be prolonged indefinitely
q: You cannot prolong your life, therefore be not careless; you are past help when old age approaches.

s: monk wins enlightenment (after caring for life)
q: First he must bestow care on his life till he wins the stake (viz. enlightenment), and afterwards he should despise it, annihilating his sins.

s: monk despises life (after winning enlightenment)
q: First he must bestow care on his life till he wins the stake (viz. enlightenment), and afterwards he should despise it, annihilating his sins.

s: will is conquered by monk
q: By conquering his will, (a monk) reaches liberation, as a well-broken horse which is clad in harness (goes to battle).

s: monk reaches liberation (by conquering the will)
q: By conquering his will, (a monk) reaches liberation, as a well-broken horse which is clad in harness (goes to battle).

s: young years facilitate liberation (when one is watchful)
q: Be watchful in your young years; for thereby a monk quickly obtains liberation.

s: old age approaches human life
q: You cannot prolong your life, therefore be not careless; you are past help when old age approaches.

s: dissolution of the body approaches human life (when life draws to its close)
q: But such a man despairs when his life draws to its close, and the dissolution of his body approaches.

s: Sramana suppresses delusion (again and again)
q: A Sramana who again and again suppresses the effects of delusion, and controls himself, will be affected in a rough way by external things; but a monk should not hate them in his mind.

s: carelessness should not be careless (because life cannot be prolonged)
q: You cannot prolong your life, therefore be not careless; you are past help when old age approaches.

s: Sramana controls himself (again and again)
q: A Sramana who again and again suppresses the effects of delusion, and controls himself, will be affected in a rough way by external things; but a monk should not hate them in his mind.

s: Sramana is affected by external things (in a rough way)
q: A Sramana who again and again suppresses the effects of delusion, and controls himself, will be affected in a rough way by external things; but a monk should not hate them in his mind.

s: external things weaken intellect
q: External things weaken the intellect and allure many; therefore keep them out of your mind.

s: external things allure many
q: External things weaken the intellect and allure many; therefore keep them out of your mind.

s: delusion is to be kept out of mind
q: External things weaken the intellect and allure many; therefore keep them out of your mind. Keep off delusion, remove pride, do not practise deceit, leave off greed.

s: heretics are impure Impurity
q: Heretics who are impure and vain, are always subject to love and hate, and are wholly under the influence (of their passions).

s: heretics are vain vanity
q: Heretics who are impure and vain, are always subject to love and hate, and are wholly under the influence (of their passions).

s: men adhering to wrong principles acquire wealth (by evil deeds)
q: Men who adhering to wrong principles acquire wealth by evil deeds, will lose it, falling into the snares (of their passions) and being held captive by their hatred.

s: heretics are subject to passions (always, through love and hate)
q: Heretics who are impure and vain, are always subject to love and hate, and are wholly under the influence (of their passions).

s: heretics is despised as unholy men
q: Despising them as unholy men, desire virtues till the end of your life.

s: men adhering to wrong principles lose wealth (through their passions and hatred)
q: Men who adhering to wrong principles acquire wealth by evil deeds, will lose it, falling into the snares (of their passions) and being held captive by their hatred.

s: passions ensnare men adhering to wrong principles
q: Men who adhering to wrong principles acquire wealth by evil deeds, will lose it, falling into the snares (of their passions) and being held captive by their hatred.

s: hatred holds captive men adhering to wrong principles
q: Men who adhering to wrong principles acquire wealth by evil deeds, will lose it, falling into the snares (of their passions) and being held captive by their hatred.

s: burglar perishes by actions (when caught in the breach of the wall)
q: As the burglar caught in the breach of the wall perishes by the work the sinner himself had executed, thus people in this life and the next cannot escape the effect of their own actions.

s: actions have effects people (in this life and the next)
q: As the burglar caught in the breach of the wall perishes by the work the sinner himself had executed, thus people in this life and the next cannot escape the effect of their own actions.

s: death against one's will is a death (a way of life ending with death)
q: These two ways of life ending with death have been declared: death with one's will, and death against one's will.

s: ignorant men does cruel actions (very cruel)
q: Mahâvîra has (thus) described the first kind in which an ignorant man, being attached to pleasures, does very cruel actions.

s: pleasures and amusements leads to the trap (of deceit)
q: A man attached to pleasures and amusements will be caught in the trap (of deceit).

s: pleasures and amusements causes grief (through attachment to them)
q: The fool boasts: 'I shall have the company of (most) men.' But by his love of pleasures and amusements he will come to grief.

s: ignorant men acts against living beings (cruelly)
q: Then he begins to act cruelly against movable and immovable beings, and he kills living beings with a purpose or without.

s: ignorant men accumulates sins (in two ways)
q: Overbearing in acts and words, desirous for wealth and women, he accumulates sins in two ways, just as a young snake gathers dust (both on and in its body).

s: sins is accumulated by ignorant men (in two ways)
q: Overbearing in acts and words, desirous for wealth and women, he accumulates sins in two ways, just as a young snake gathers dust (both on and in its body).

s: ignorant men suffers from disease
q: Then he suffers ill and is attacked by disease; and he is in dread of the next world when he reflects on his deeds.

s: rebirth is determined by sins (according to one's deeds)
q: Then going to the place where he is to be born again according to his deeds, he feels remorse, as I have heard (from my teacher).

s: death against one's will is experienced by ignorant men
q: Death against one's will is that of ignorant men, and it happens (to the same individual) many times.

s: virtuous man experiences death (while controlling themselves and subduing their senses)
q: Full of peace and without injury to any one is, as I have heard (from my teachers), the death of the virtuous who control themselves and subdue their senses.

s: monk possesses morality (not always good throughout)
q: Such a death) does not fall to the lot of every monk, nor of every householder; for the morality of householders is of various character, and that of monks is not always good throughout.

s: householders possesses morality (of various character)
q: Such a death) does not fall to the lot of every monk, nor of every householder; for the morality of householders is of various character, and that of monks is not always good throughout.

s: saints surpasses householders (in self-control)
q: Some householders are superior to some monks in self-control; but the saints are superior to all householders in self-control.

s: Self-control is superior in saints (compared with all householders)
q: Some householders are superior to some monks in self-control; but the saints are superior to all householders in self-control.

s: monk can be sinners (despite being mendicants)
q: A sinner, though he be a mendicant (friar), will not escape hell; but a pious man, whether monk or householder, ascends to heaven.

s: death against one's will occurs repeatedly many times (to the same individual)
q: Death against one's will is that of ignorant men, and it happens (to the same individual) many times.

s: householders should practise rules of conduct (as faithful people)
q: A faithful man should practise the rules of conduct for householders; he should never neglect the Pôsaha fast in both fortnights, not even for a single night.

s: householders should observe Pôsaha fast (in both fortnights)
q: A faithful man should practise the rules of conduct for householders; he should never neglect the Pôsaha fast in both fortnights, not even for a single night.

s: Pôsaha fast is observed by householders (in both fortnights)
q: A faithful man should practise the rules of conduct for householders; he should never neglect the Pôsaha fast in both fortnights, not even for a single night.

s: householders shares Yakshas (when living piously under discipline and quitting flesh and bones)
q: When under such discipline he lives piously even as a householder, he will, on quitting flesh and bones, share the world of the Yakshas.

s: Yakshas has world the world
q: When under such discipline he lives piously even as a householder, he will, on quitting flesh and bones, share the world of the Yakshas.

s: monk can become liberated (when restrained)
q: Now a restrained monk will become one of the two: either one free from all misery or a god of great power.

s: monk can become heaven (when trained in self-control and penance)
q: To the highest regions, in due order, to those where there is no delusion, and to those which are full of light, where the glorious (gods dwell)--who have long life, great power, great lustre, who can change their shape at will, who are beautiful as on their first day, and have the brilliancy of many suns--to such places go those who are trained in self-control and penance, monks or householders, who have obtained liberation by absence of passion.

s: householders can obtain liberation (through self-control, penance, and absence of passion)
q: To the highest regions, in due order, to those where there is no delusion, and to those which are full of light, where the glorious (gods dwell)--who have long life, great power, great lustre, who can change their shape at will, who are beautiful as on their first day, and have the brilliancy of many suns--to such places go those who are trained in self-control and penance, monks or householders, who have obtained liberation by absence of passion.

s: liberation is obtained by Self-control (with penance and absence of passion)
q: To the highest regions, in due order, to those where there is no delusion, and to those which are full of light, where the glorious (gods dwell)--who have long life, great power, great lustre, who can change their shape at will, who are beautiful as on their first day, and have the brilliancy of many suns--to such places go those who are trained in self-control and penance, monks or householders, who have obtained liberation by absence of passion.

s: death with one's will is a death (a way of life ending with death)
q: These two ways of life ending with death have been declared: death with one's will, and death against one's will.

s: Law is transgressed by ignorant men (in embracing unrighteousness)
q: so the fool, who transgresses the Law and embraces unrighteousness, repents in the hour of death, like (the charioteer) over the broken axle.

s: unrighteousness is embraced by ignorant men (in transgression of the Law)
q: so the fool, who transgresses the Law and embraces unrighteousness, repents in the hour of death, like (the charioteer) over the broken axle.

s: Law of Compassion teaches the better one
q: A wise man having weighed (both kinds of death) and chosen the better one (taught in) the Law of Compassion, will become calm through patience, with an undisturbed mind (at the time of death).

s: death preparation is practised by monk (when the right time has arrived)
q: When the right time (to prepare for death) has arrived, a faithful (monk) should in the presence (of his teacher) suppress all emotions (of fear or joy) and wait for the dissolution of his body.

s: death preparation requires Self-control (suppression of fear and joy)
q: When the right time (to prepare for death) has arrived, a faithful (monk) should in the presence (of his teacher) suppress all emotions (of fear or joy) and wait for the dissolution of his body.

s: death with one's will is reached by wise people (through one of the three methods)
q: When the time for quitting the body has come, a sage dies the 'death with one's will,' according to one of the three methods.

s: death with one's will is experienced by wise people
q: Death against one's will is that of ignorant men, and it happens (to the same individual) many times. Death with one's will is that of wise men, and at best it happens but once.

s: death with one's will occurs repeatedly once (at best)
q: Death against one's will is that of ignorant men, and it happens (to the same individual) many times. Death with one's will is that of wise men, and at best it happens but once.

s: Mahâvîra describes death against one's will (as the first kind of death)
q: Mahâvîra has (thus) described the first kind in which an ignorant man, being attached to pleasures, does very cruel actions.

s: ignorant men is a men
q: Death against one's will is that of ignorant men, and it happens (to the same individual) many times.

s: ignorant men is attached to pleasures and amusements
q: Mahâvîra has (thus) described the first kind in which an ignorant man, being attached to pleasures, does very cruel actions.

s: The False Ascetic is a ascetic
q: The False Ascetic.

s: creatures are not deprived of human life (because they love their own self)
q: therefore, knowing the creatures' love of their own self, do not deprive them of their life, but cease from endangering and combating them.

s: presents lead to hell (when accepted)
q: Seeing that to accept (presents) leads to hell, one should not accept even a blade of grass;

s: alms-bowl contains food (put there for preserving one's life)
q: only to preserve one's life one should eat the food that is put in one's own alms-bowl.

s: teacher is attended by some people seeking deliverance from misery (without abstaining from sins)
q: Here some are of opinion that they will be delivered from all misery by merely attending the teacher, without abstaining from sins.

s: sin cause sinking lower and lower (through the endless Samsâra)
q: Fools, though sinking lower and lower through their sins, believe themselves to be wise men.

s: liberation is beyond this world (as the chosen goal)
q: Choosing what is beyond and above (this world, viz. liberation), one should never desire (worldly objects),

s: Karman is annihilated by sustaining one's body (as the purpose of sustaining the body)
q: but sustain one's body only to be able to annihilate one's Karman.

s: Death is awaited by an ascetic (while wandering after recognising the cause of Karman)
q: Recognising the cause of Karman, one should wander about waiting for one's death;

s: food and drink has permitted quantity (for an ascetic)
q: (knowing) the permitted quantity of food and drink, one should eat (such food as has been) prepared (by the householders for their own consumption).

s: alms-bowl is carried by an ascetic (without desires, like a bird with its plumage)
q: but as a bird with its plumage, so he with his alms-bowl should wander about without desires.

s: Arhat Gñâtriputra is a Arhat (venerable native of Vaisâlî)
q: Thus has spoken the Arhat Gñâtriputra, the venerable native of Vaisâlî,

s: Arhat Gñâtriputra is native of Vaisâlî (venerable)
q: Thus has spoken the Arhat Gñâtriputra, the venerable native of Vaisâlî,

s: Arhat Gñâtriputra possesses highest knowledge (highest)
q: who possesses the highest knowledge and who possesses the highest faith,

s: Arhat Gñâtriputra possesses highest faith (highest)
q: who possesses the highest knowledge and who possesses the highest faith,

s: householders prepare food (for their own consumption)
q: one should eat (such food as has been) prepared (by the householders for their own consumption).

s: pain affects all men ignorant of Truth (throughout endless Samsâra)
q: All men who are ignorant of the Truth are subject to pain; in the endless Samsâra they suffer in many ways.

s: Samsâra is a endless cycle
q: in the endless Samsâra they suffer in many ways.

s: bondage leads to birth (through its ways)
q: Therefore a wise man, who considers well the ways that lead to bondage and birth, should himself search for the truth, and be kind towards all creatures.

s: creatures love their own self
q: Everything that happens to somebody, affects him personally; therefore, knowing the creatures' love of their own self, do not deprive them of their life, but cease from endangering and combating them.

s: Seventh Lecture is a lecture
q: Seventh Lecture.

s: ignorant great sinner tells lies
q: An ignorant man kills, tells lies, robs on the highway, steals foreign goods, deceives, (always thinking of some one) whom he could plunder, the villain. (5)

s: ignorant great sinner robs on the highway
q: An ignorant man kills, tells lies, robs on the highway, steals foreign goods, deceives, (always thinking of some one) whom he could plunder, the villain. (5)
